title: Finite homogeneous generators of a finitely generated graded module
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1], graded by total degree (S_d is the k-span of monomials of total degree d, and S_d=0 for d<0), with the projective-line convention [def-sc-p1-standard]. Every finitely generated Z-graded S-module M has a finite homogeneous generating set m_1,...,m_r; consequently the graded map F_0=direct sum_{j=1}^r S(-deg m_j) \to M (S(e) the shifted graded module [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (2)) sending the j-th basis vector to m_j is a surjective graded S-linear map.

source.place: proof, construction of the initial graded free module from homogeneous generators

proof.text: Let H be the set of elements lying in some graded piece. Choose the direct-sum decomposition from hℳ. DirectSum.Decomposition.inductionOn shows every element belongs to the S-span of H: zero belongs, each homogeneous element is a span generator, and the span is closed under addition. Thus span S H = top. Module.Finite.fg_top and Submodule.fg_span_iff_fg_span_finset_subset extract a finite subset of H with the same span. Enumerate it by a Fin r embedding using Set.Finite.fin_embedding and choose a degree for each generator. This is the finite homogeneous generating family.

source.place: proof, construction of the initial graded free module from homogeneous generators

proof.text: Take Finsupp.linearCombination S m as the map from Fin r →₀ S to M. By span_range_eq_top_iff_surjective_finsuppLinearCombination its surjectivity follows from the spanning equality. Finsupp.linearCombination_single and one_smul show its value on the ith basis vector is m i.

source.place: proof, construction of the initial graded free module from homogeneous generators

proof.text: For a homogeneous scalar s of degree n, linearity and the basis-vector computation give f (s • single i 1) = s • m i. Apply the stated compatibility hsmul with m i in graded degree d i to obtain membership in degree n + d i. This expresses the shift convention directly, without using the twisting-sheaf construction.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_homogeneous_generators {k : Type u} [Field k] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) M] [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) M] (ℳ : ℤ → AddSubgroup M) (hℳ : DirectSum.IsInternal ℳ) (hsmul : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : ℤ) (s : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (x : M), s ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n → x ∈ ℳ j → s • x ∈ ℳ ((n : ℤ) + j)) : ∃ (r : ℕ) (d : Fin r → ℤ) (m : Fin r → M) (hm : ∀ i, m i ∈ ℳ (d i)) (f : (Fin r →₀ MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) →ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k] M), Function.Surjective f ∧ (∀ i, f (Finsupp.single i 1) = m i) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin r) (n : ℕ) (s : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k), s ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n → f (s • Finsupp.single i 1) ∈ ℳ ((n : ℤ) + d i))
